analyses.failure: test_chk_014_nominal_latency — CHK-013: i_full_thr=depth expected o_full_thr=0 got 1 at 1680691 ps (fails in 11 of 12 runs; SVA a_CHK_013 also fires: sim.log:249 'NNC_FAIL CHK-013 @1681000')
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:524 CHK-013(c): "if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy)". Spec REQ-FUNC-010 (rules.json:659, AF-3-14): "o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr ... it is pessimistic for the full side (it can be larger than the true occupancy)". rules.json:13573 (designer answer): the estimate "differs from the true occupancy only by pointer updates still inside the synchronizer". Contract CHK-014 stimulus (contract.json:560): "Metastability model off, i_empty_thr=0, i_full_thr=8". Model semantics: spec:653 / DEC-012 spec:1479 "The model randomizes the latency of each bit independently ... 0, 1, or 2 extra cycles"; spec:684 assumes "A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value"; DEC-023 spec:1491 "the destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency".
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:106 o_full uses Gray equality (reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ MSK); :112-120 converts w_rgray_s to binary and w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s (mod 16); :126 o_full_thr = w_occ >= i_full_thr. With a coherent synchronized pointer, w_occ is in 0..8 and (w_occ>=8) == w_full_n, so CHK-013(c) cannot fail. It fails only when w_occ is 9..15, i.e. w_rbin_s is AHEAD of reg_wbin. The synchronizer is m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv:46-56: one independent m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync per bit. Its simulation model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182) gives each bit its own random extra delay of 0..2 cycles (:161). If bit A changes at destination edge k with extra=2 (visible k+2), and bit B changes at edge k+1 with extra=0 (visible k+1), the output at k+1 is a Gray word the source never held. Example: read Gray 0001(1)->0011(2) shows 0010 = binary 3 while the true read pointer is 2. With the FIFO drained (wbin=2), w_occ = 2-3 = 15 gives o_full_thr=1 and o_full=0. That is the observed failure. Test 014 uses wr 14 ns / rd 6 ns (sim.log:47): the read pointer moves about 2.3 counts per write edge during the drain, so Gray bits change at consecutive write edges, which is the case that triggers the reordering. Every run uses the model: sim.log:37 '+AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=1', sim.log:47 'exact=False'. No run in sim_runs/ has exact=True or MSYNC_EN=0 (grep: 0 matches).
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:861-906: Env(per, ft=DEPTH, et=0). Ten times: single write into the empty FIFO, fill to 8, one read, drain at the read clock (drain() :477-485). The monitor (_on_w :196-216) checks at every write edge. At :212-214, with ft==DEPTH and sb_on, exp = int(full==1 and sw==1 and busy==0), taken directly from contract CHK-013(c). Here it sampled o_full=0, sw=1, busy=0, so exp=0, but o_full_thr=1. The test sees EXACT=False (:44) and only logs NNC_NOT_VERIFIABLE (:871-872). It still runs with the model on, although contract.json:560 asks for the model off.

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model follows DEC-012 literally: independent per-bit latency with up to +2 cycles (cell_sync.sv:92-93, :161). The spec assumes this can only show the previous pointer value (spec:684) or valid Gray values (DEC-023 spec:1491). That assumption is false when a pointer advances at consecutive destination edges (fast source): a bit delayed by 2 can be overtaken by a later bit delayed by 0, so an incoherent value appears, with w_occ > DEPTH. REQ-FUNC-010 (AF-3-14), the pessimism rule (rules.json:13573) and TEST-008 "flags never optimistic" (spec:1246) then cannot all hold with the DEC-012 model. Failures appear in every model-on run and seed (base.s1..s5, cell1/3/4, macro, rd/wr_slow) and for S=2,3,4. CHK-015, which uses only isolated single updates, passes.
candidates.evidence_against: No run with the model disabled or with VLSIT_SYNTHESIS exists in this run set, so it is not proven that the failure disappears without the model. No waveform of w_rgray_s exists to confirm the incoherent value at 1680691 ps.

candidates.evidence_for: The model is RTL (rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv) and is the source of the incoherent synchronized pointer. A physical 2-FF synchronizer samples all bits at one instant and resolves at most the one bit that is toggling. It never presents a value the source did not hold, so this model is not faithful to the hardware it stands for. The flag logic (wr.sv:120,126) also has no protection against w_occ > DEPTH.
candidates.evidence_against: cell_sync.sv implements exactly what DEC-012 / spec 10.6.4 ask for (per-bit independence, 0/1/2 extra cycles, replace-and-restart). The flag equation wr.sv:126 matches REQ-FUNC-010. With a coherent pointer, CHK-013(c) holds by construction (Gray full == binary occ 8).

candidates.evidence_for: contract.json:560 requires 'Metastability model off' for CHK-014, but the run passes +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=1 (sim.log:37) and the test continues with the model on (py:871-872). In the contracted configuration the failure would most likely not occur.
candidates.evidence_against: The failing check is CHK-013, which the contract applies at every edge in every run, including model-on runs that the contract itself requires (CHK-016 contract.json:606-607, CHK-029 :934-935). The expected value (py:213) is a faithful copy of CHK-013(c) and agrees with the SVA (nnc_chk_wr.sv:122-127), which fails at the same time.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify the spec, then fix the RTL model. Option a: limit the per-bit extra delay so it cannot reorder bits (with at most +1 cycle at the last stage, the mix of two consecutive samples is still a valid Gray value); this means changing DEC-012 and the S+2 window of CHK-015/AF-10.3-02. Option b: randomize at the first-stage capture, and only for the bit that toggles at that instant. Option c: move the model to vector level in m_vlsit_afifo_sync, which needs a change to DEC-038/039. (2) Fix the test/run set: run CHK-014 with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 as contract.json:560 requires. This makes this test match its contract but does not remove the conflict seen in CHK-016/029. (3) Discriminating experiment before deciding: rerun base.s1 with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 and with +define+VLSIT_SYNTHESIS, and add a debug assertion that each change of w_rgray_s/w_wgray_s is a valid forward Gray step (binary value non-decreasing mod 2^PW and not ahead of the source pointer). Do not mask the issue by saturating w_occ in wr.sv:126.

With i_empty_thr=13 (sim.log:69), o_empty_thr=0 needs w_occ = 14 or 15, i.e. the synchronized write pointer is 1-2 counts BEHIND the read pointer. A coherent synchronizer can never produce this, because the read pointer advances only while reg_rgray != w_wgray_s (:97,100). The per-bit model (cell_sync.sv:149-182, :161) can produce it. Example: write Gray 0111(5)->0101(6)->0100(7); bit1 delayed 2 and bit0 delayed 0 give 0110 = binary 4 after 5 was already seen. The synchronized pointer steps backwards, so w_occ = 4-5 = 15 and o_empty_thr=0. Clocks are 10/10.3 ns, so pointer bits change at consecutive destination edges during bursts.

CHK-016 explicitly requires the model on and CHK-003 to never fail (contract.json:606-607), so the spec asks for two incompatible things.

The read domain therefore believes in more words than were written: w_wbin_s is ahead of the real write pointer. Clocks are 10/37 ns (sim.log:172), so the write pointer advances about 3.7 counts per read edge and several Gray bits change at consecutive read edges. The per-bit independent +0..2 delay (cell_sync.sv:158-169) can then present a Gray code ahead of the source (for example 0001->0011 seen as 0010 = 3 when the true value is 2).

Reference: _on_w moves Q to P at the request edge (py:233-236); _on_r pops P/Q on accepted reads (py:284-291), clears P after S+3 read edges (py:269-273) per contract CHK-005 (contract.json:342), and occ = len(Q)+len(P) (py:274). candidates.evidence_for: An optimistic empty-side estimate is exactly what an incoherent synchronized write pointer produces. With a 3.7:1 clock ratio the DEC-012 model (spec:1479) reorders bit updates often. It fails only in some seeds/configs (6 of 12), which fits a random event. The spec claims the model only delays (spec:684) and that only valid Gray values are seen (DEC-023 spec:1491), and both claims are false for this model.
candidates.evidence_against: No model-off run of CHK-029 exists, although contract.json:934 requires one. A TB reference-model error around software-reset windows is also possible (see B).

candidates.evidence_for: The reference occupancy around a software reset depends on the TB's P bookkeeping (py:233-236, 269-273): P is cleared after S+3 read edges and the request edge is taken as p_t. If the RTL estimate legitimately includes words that the TB has already moved or cleared, occ could be undercounted. With the model, the read block can arrive up to S+2 edges after the request (LMAX, py:45), close to the S+3 clear point.
candidates.evidence_against: P is only cleared at S+3 = 5 (S=2) or later, after the latest block arrival at S+2 per spec:517, so the TB window is consistent with the contract (contract.json:342). An undercount would also normally fire CHK-005/CHK-006 data checks, and none of those fail (sim.log:303-304, 0 fails). The same optimistic-flag signature appears in non-reset tests (regression full side).

candidates.evidence_for: The model in rtl/ yields an optimistic flag, which violates TEST-008 (spec:1246) and REQ-FUNC-009/010 in simulation.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows DEC-012. The flag equation follows REQ-FUNC-010.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify DEC-012/10.6.4 to require coherent synchronized values, then fix cell_sync.sv (bounded +1 per bit, capture-time randomization, or a vector-level model with a DEC-038/039 change). (2) Add the model-off CHK-029 run required by contract.json:934. If that run fails too, examine the TB P/Q window (py:233-236, 269-273) against the RTL request latency. analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-010 AF-3-14 rules.json:659: the write-domain estimate "is pessimistic for the full side (it can be larger than the true occupancy)". contract.json:982 CHK-032: "The flag is never on the optimistic side of the true occupancy." analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:120,126: o_full_thr = (reg_wbin - w_rbin_s) >= 5. Got 0 while the true occupancy is 5, so w_occ <= 4: the write domain believes the read pointer is further ahead than it really is. A correct synchronizer only lags the source, so w_rbin_s ahead of the true read pointer requires an incoherent synchronized value. The per-bit model (cell_sync.sv:158-169, extra = rs % 3 at :161) can produce one when read-pointer bits change at consecutive write edges (for example read Gray 0001->0011 shown as 0010 = 3 when the true value is 2).
analyses.test_does: py:1717-1738: Env(None, ft=randint=5, et=randint=8), Traffic, random_traffic 800, sw_random 8, random_traffic 300, then hw_reset and more traffic. _on_w py:229-239: n = len(Q) (accepted writes minus reads accepted at read edges up to now); if sw=1, busy=0 and n >= i_full_thr, then o_full_thr must be 1.

candidates.evidence_for: This is an optimistic full-side estimate, the direct signature of a synchronized read pointer running ahead, which the DEC-012 per-bit model can create (spec:1479). It contradicts spec:684 and DEC-023 spec:1491 ('only valid Gray values'). It fails across seeds and cell types.
candidates.evidence_against: No model-off evidence. The traceback snippet (results message) does not show the failing write edge's pointer state.

candidates.evidence_for: The TB counts reads at read edges up to the current time. A read at a read edge at the same timestamp as the write edge could be counted, but the design cannot yet see it. That would make n smaller, not larger, so it would not cause this failure. A P/Q handling slip after sw_random (py:233-236) could leave Q overcounted if words that the RTL discarded were left in Q.
candidates.evidence_against: Q is moved to P at the request edge (py:233-236), so discarded words are not in Q. No CHK-005/CHK-006 scoreboard failure is reported, which would accompany a Q overcount at a full FIFO (CHK-006 at py:231-232 would expect o_full=1).

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model makes the full-side flag optimistic, violating REQ-FUNC-008/010 in simulation.
candidates.evidence_against: It matches DEC-012 as written. The flag logic matches REQ-FUNC-010.

analyses.rtl_does: rd.sv:117 o_empty = rd_blk | (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s); :118 o_empty_thr = rd_blk ? 1 : (w_wbin_s - reg_rbin <= i_empty_thr).
